summary.text: Writing as Deputy Secretary of Labor on November 24, 2025, Sonderling described AI as an opportunity for workers and encouraged its adoption for higher-paying jobs, productivity, and greater personal fulfillment. On February 27, 2025, he emphasized that workplace AI should comply with existing civil-rights and health-and-safety laws, describing both potential workplace benefits and discrimination risks. He also called for reskilling workers displaced by AI, including knowledge workers whose jobs had historically been performed in offices.

statements.text: We have to look at this in various ways. The first and foremost position is that any use of artificial intelligence in the workforce, and something, obviously, I'm very passionate about, complies with longstanding laws or it's civil rights laws, whether it's health and safety laws, to ensure that it's being used properly on the American workforce to actually help make them more productive, help make their jobs better, safer, more secure. And there's a lot of promise with AI on that. But on the flip side, if we don't have those American values built into it, if we don't have those civil rights protections built into artificial intelligence, not only are people potentially going to be discriminate, but the products are not going to be able to do what they are intended to do.
